newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turk MPs to begin anti-government censure debate.
newsitem.headline: Turk MPs to begin anti-government censure debate.

text.p: Turkey's parliament will on Tuesday begin debating an opposition censure motion against the Islamist-led government, parliament speaker Mustafa Kalemli told reporters.
"The preliminary censure debate will take place today. If it is decided at this session that the censure motion will be taken up, the full debate will be on Thursday," Kalemli said.
The opposition motion requires a simple majority of those in parliament in order to go forward to the full debate on Thursday and a further vote on Saturday.

An absolute majority of 276 is needed to bring down the government in the final vote, but according to Turkey's parliamentary tradition, the government would be expected to resign if it lost the vote on Tuesday.
The government of Islamist Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan, which has 280 seats in the 550-seat parliament, has survived three censure motions since it was formed in June.
The opposition has said it expects many government MPs to support the motion, which effectively serves as a no-confidence motion against the government.

Deputy Prime Minister Tansu Ciller met one by one with several dissident MPs in her conservative party on Tuesday in a bid to persuade them to support the government, the state-run Anatolian news agency said.
